entries.summary: Linh Ung Pagoda is the Son Tra stop where temple courtyards, incense, sea wind, and the white Lady Buddha all sit above Da Nang's coast.
entries.context: The visit feels strongest when the view is not the whole point. Move through the grounds like an active religious place, then let the coast open around it.
entries.tip: Chua Linh Ung is the pagoda name to recognize. Many visitors say Lady Buddha for the same area, but the pagoda gives the statue its setting.
entries.rationale: Linh Ung gives Da Nang a coastal spiritual stop that is neither only a viewpoint nor only a statue photo.

sections.title: Temple Grounds Before The View
sections.body: Linh Ung Pagoda sits high on Son Tra, where courtyards, incense, sea wind, and Lady Buddha come together above Da Nang. The view is part of the visit, but the place still asks for temple manners.

sections.title: Move Like It Is Active
sections.body: Dress and walk as if people are there to pray, not only to take photos. Lower voices, give space around incense and altars, and let the courtyard set the pace.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Say Chua Linh Ung for the pagoda. It often appears beside Lady Buddha and Son Tra, keeping the temple, statue, and peninsula in the same mental picture.

sections.title: The Statue Sets The Scale
sections.body: Lady Buddha gives the complex its strongest visual pull. Find the statue, then look back toward the city and coast to understand why this pagoda feels tied to the peninsula.

sections.title: Temple Manners First
sections.body: Arrive ready for a working pagoda, not only a viewpoint. Covered shoulders, quieter voices, and slower movement make the statue and sea view feel connected to the temple grounds.

sections.title: Son Tra Can Wait
sections.body: The pagoda pairs naturally with a Son Tra drive, but it does not need to become a rushed checklist. If weather, road, or group energy feels off, the grounds and view are enough.

entries.summary: Long Coffee is an old-school Da Nang cafe pause: low stools, iced glasses, metal phin coffee, and a short reset between hotter plans.
entries.context: This is a coffee stop to sit inside for a little while, not a whole afternoon to perform. The room, ice, and street rhythm do the work.
entries.tip: Start with ca phe sua da for sweet and strong, or ca phe den da if you want the coffee darker and less softened.
entries.rationale: Long Coffee adds a grounded cafe rhythm to the Da Nang set without pretending every pause needs a major attraction around it.

sections.title: Sit Low And Let The Coffee Work
sections.body: Long Coffee is for the pause: low stools, iced glasses, metal phin coffee, and a room that keeps moving without asking much from you. Come between bigger plans, not as a laptop afternoon.

sections.title: Order Simply
sections.body: Choose ca phe sua da if you want the classic sweet, strong version. Choose ca phe den da if you want the coffee darker and less softened.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Ca phe Long is the local name to notice on maps or signs. Keep it tied to the old-school coffee table, not a generic cafe stop.

sections.title: Stay For The Street Rhythm
sections.body: The point is the table, the ice, the phin, the small talk, and the way people come and go. It can still be memorable because nothing needs to perform.

sections.title: Old-School Coffee Pause
sections.body: Good for a short, local-feeling coffee stop when the day needs shade and caffeine more than a polished cafe plan. The point is the stool-side rhythm.

sections.title: One Coffee, Then Back Out
sections.body: Keep the stop short enough to stay pleasant. After one coffee and a little shade, move back into the day before heat, traffic, or another plan takes over.

entries.summary: Lotte Mart Da Nang is the cool indoor errand stop for water, sunscreen, toiletries, snacks, simple clothes, and a calmer pickup plan.
entries.context: It earns its place when the day is hot, rainy, or low on supplies, with predictable shelves and posted prices instead of market texture.
entries.tip: Go to Han Market for bargaining, fabric, food counters, and local noise. Come here for air conditioning, receipts, and fewer small problems.
entries.rationale: Lotte Mart gives the Da Nang library a practical restock stop that differs clearly from markets, night markets, and souvenir browsing.

sections.title: A Cool-Aisle Reset
sections.body: Lotte Mart Da Nang is the clean indoor errand stop for the part of the day when water, sunscreen, tissues, snacks, or a backup shirt matter more than atmosphere.

sections.title: Bring The Ordinary List
sections.body: This is where the unglamorous things belong: water, sunscreen, toiletries, tissues, snacks, simple clothes, small gifts. It is useful before the beach, a ride south, or a room reset.

sections.title: Cool Down Before The Car
sections.body: If the group is fading, take a few minutes inside before choosing the next move. Bags, water, and a clear pickup point make the taxi feel less scrambled.

sections.title: Market Texture Is Elsewhere
sections.body: For bargaining, fabric, food counters, and local-market noise, go to Han Market. Lotte is for posted prices, bright shelves, receipts, and lower decision pressure.

entries.summary: Love Bridge is a quick Han River pause near Dragon Bridge, with heart lanterns, lock railings, the Dragon Carp statue, and one easy evening photo frame.
entries.context: Treat it as a small link in a river walk, not the center of the night. The stop makes most sense when you are already nearby.
entries.tip: Take the river angle, decide quickly about a lock, then fold the stop into Dragon Bridge, APEC Park, Son Tra Night Market, or a slow Han River walk.
entries.rationale: Love Bridge earns its place as a short, sentimental riverfront stop that ties the evening route together.

sections.title: A Five-Minute River Pause
sections.body: Love Bridge is a quick Han River stop near Dragon Bridge: heart lanterns, lock-covered railings, the Dragon Carp statue nearby, and one easy photo frame before the evening moves on.

sections.title: Sweet, Not Subtle
sections.body: The bridge is romantic in an obvious way. That is fine. Give it a few minutes, take the river angle, and leave before the pose starts feeling bigger than the place.

sections.title: Locks Need A Check
sections.body: If a lock matters, confirm where to buy one and whether current rules allow it. Otherwise, the railing, lanterns, and river view are enough.

sections.title: Fold It Into The Walk
sections.body: Pair the stop with Dragon Bridge, the Dragon Carp statue, APEC Park, Son Tra Night Market, or a slow Han River walk. It is strongest as part of the loop.

entries.summary: Madame Lan is a polished Da Nang dinner stop for courtyard light, shared plates, a clearer menu, and a meal that can hold its own place in the night.
entries.context: A calmer dinner fit than a quick bite between river plans. Keep the order flexible and let the room, table pace, and menu in front of you guide the meal.
entries.tip: Read the menu before ordering wide. One main and one shared plate can make the table easier before adding more.
entries.rationale: Madame Lan brings restaurant rhythm, room, and Han River evening context into the city set through shared plates and a calmer night pace.

sections.title: Dinner With A Room Around It
sections.body: Madame Lan is the Da Nang restaurant to choose when dinner becomes part of the night, not just a stop between Han River plans.

sections.title: Read Before Ordering Wide
sections.body: The room makes it tempting to order too much. Choose one main, one vegetable or shared plate, then see the table size before adding more.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Madame Lan may be the name you hear first. Keep it tied to courtyard, lantern light, and shared-plate pacing rather than a single promised dish.

sections.title: Courtyard Time Beats A Rush
sections.body: If you land near the lanterned courtyard, give the meal a little time. This is one of the easier places in Da Nang to let dinner feel like a pause.

sections.title: Dinner With A Little Space
sections.body: A good fit when the meal needs to feel calmer than a quick bite between river plans. Keep the order flexible and let the table pace the night.

sections.title: When The Group Needs Range
sections.body: It suits a group with different confidence levels: people who want Vietnamese food, someone who wants a clearer menu, and anyone tired of negotiating every detail.

entries.summary: Man Thai Beach is a quieter Da Nang coastal scene, with fishing boats, Son Tra hills, working sand, and a better reason to go early.
entries.context: This is not the easiest all-day beach setup. It works as a short walk, photo pause, or seafood-side detour when the coast still feels local.
entries.tip: Go light, keep out of working space, and choose a pickup point before wandering away from the main road.
entries.rationale: Man Thai Beach adds a working-coast note to Da Nang's beach set: fishing boats, quieter sand, Son Tra edges, and a short coastal pause.

sections.title: Fishing Boats Before The Beach Day
sections.body: Man Thai Beach is the beach scene to picture before Da Nang turns into hotel towers and sunbeds: fishing boats on sand, Son Tra hills behind them, and the morning still quiet.

sections.title: Early Light, Working Sand
sections.body: Morning is when the boats and light make the place feel specific. Walk gently, keep out of working space, and treat the beach as more than a backdrop.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Bien Man Thai is the beach name to notice. It keeps the stop closer to the fishing edge than to the better-known hotel beach image.

sections.title: Not The Easiest All-Day Setup
sections.body: For loungers, hotel services, and a more familiar swim plan, another beach may be easier. Man Thai is better as a short coastal pause or photo walk.

sections.title: Fishing Edge Morning
sections.body: Good as a quiet coastal look before the beach day gets busy. Come for boats, Son Tra edges, and sea air rather than a full-service swim stop.

sections.title: A Pickup Pin Before Wandering
sections.body: The beach can feel quiet once you step away from the main road. Drop a pin before wandering and choose the pickup point while everyone still has energy.

entries.summary: The Marble Mountain cave walk is the cave-and-shrine layer of Ngu Hanh Son, with stone steps, dimmer air, incense, and a slower kind of attention.

entries.tip: Treat shrine spaces differently from viewpoints. Lower your voice, watch signs, and ask before taking photos when the space feels active.
entries.rationale: The cave walk gives Marble Mountains a specific on-foot rhythm, distinct from the broader mountain-cluster stop.

sections.title: Stone Steps Before Shrine Light
sections.body: The Marble Mountain cave walk is the part of Ngu Hanh Son where the city drops away: stone steps, cave shade, incense, shrine light, and a slower kind of attention than the beach road asks for.

sections.title: Cave Pace Before Photos
sections.body: This is not a flat photo stop. Expect steps, uneven stone, dimmer cave spaces, and places where quiet matters more than speed.

sections.title: Name To Recognize

sections.title: Respect The Shrine Light
sections.body: Some corners feel more like worship spaces than sightseeing stops. Lower your voice, watch signs, and put the camera away when the space calls for it.

sections.title: Caves Over Checklist
sections.body: Good when the cave-and-shrine pace matters more than racing every viewpoint. Stairs, shade, and respectful pauses shape the visit.

sections.title: Enough Without Every Viewpoint
sections.body: A cave walk can be enough if the heat or stairs start to win. Pair it with a cafe break or a ride back toward the beach instead of stacking every viewpoint.

entries.summary: Marble Mountains is a compact climb through limestone hills, caves, pagodas, stone steps, viewpoints, and carving streets south of Da Nang.
entries.context: The place asks for movement. Arrive ready to climb into the site rather than only photograph the name from below.
entries.tip: Ngu Hanh Son refers to the broader mountain cluster, so it can cover caves, pagodas, viewpoints, and the stone shops near the base.
entries.rationale: Marble Mountains combines geology, Buddhist spaces, craft streets, and coastal views in one Da Nang stop close to the beach side.

sections.title: The Climb Is The Point
sections.body: Marble Mountains is close enough to feel like a city stop, but it asks for stairs, cave air, incense, and pauses at pagoda gates. Come ready to move through it.

sections.title: Stairs Before Viewpoints
sections.body: The first stretch tells you what kind of visit this is. Stone steps, shaded rock, and temple corners slow the pace before the higher views back toward Da Nang's beach side.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Ngu Hanh Son is the local name for the five-element mountain cluster. It keeps the stop broader than one cave, one pagoda, or one photo angle.

sections.title: Caves Change The Mood
sections.body: Inside the chambers, the air drops and shrine light does more than any single photo. Move quietly, give people room, and let your eyes adjust before reaching for the camera.

sections.title: Several Stops In One Climb
sections.body: Treat the mountains as a compact climb with choices: caves, pagodas, viewpoints, and stone-carving streets below. Shoes and patience matter more than one photo.

sections.title: Stone Shops At The Base
sections.body: The streets below have stone-carving shops and traffic around the entrance area. Browse only if you have attention left; the climb itself is already enough for one compact stop.

entries.summary: Mi Quang is the Da Nang bowl to recognize by its shallow broth, turmeric noodles, herbs, peanuts, rice cracker, and texture-first rhythm.
entries.context: Dish guidance first, venue choice second. Understand the bowl before choosing a shop, protein, or add-on.
entries.tip: Pick the protein first, then taste before adding more chili. Break the rice cracker late if you want the crunch to last.
entries.rationale: Mi Quang teaches Da Nang through the bowl itself: turmeric noodles, herbs, cracker, broth, and the confidence to order by name.

sections.title: Look For The Shallow Bowl
sections.body: Mi Quang in Da Nang is not a soupy noodle bowl. It usually lands wide and shallow, with turmeric-colored noodles, a little rich broth, herbs, peanuts, and a rice cracker.

sections.title: Protein Before Extras
sections.body: Menus often split the bowl by chicken, shrimp-and-pork, or a house mix. Pick that before worrying about extras; the noodles, herbs, peanuts, and cracker are the shape.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Mi Quang is the dish name to listen for in Da Nang. The Quang part points toward central Vietnam, not a generic noodle bowl.

sections.title: Break The Cracker Late
sections.body: The rice cracker is not garnish to ignore. Break it once the bowl is in front of you, then pull herbs through the sauce so the crunch does not disappear too early.

sections.title: Bowl Before Venue
sections.body: Best before picking a restaurant or protein, so the dish itself is clear: turmeric noodles, shallow broth, herbs, peanuts, rice cracker, and sauce.

sections.title: Local Meal, Light Shape
sections.body: A good bowl sits between beach-day ease and central-Vietnam depth: dry enough to stay light, saucy enough to remember. It is a smart first local meal.

entries.summary: Mi Quang 1A is a focused Da Nang noodle stop where the useful move is simple: choose the bowl, fold in herbs, and keep lunch narrow.
entries.context: A small noodle-shop stop feels clearest when the meal stays simple. Let the bowl, herbs, cracker, and quick table rhythm carry lunch.
entries.tip: Keep the order around mi Quang first. Decide the style the menu is actually serving that day before adding extras.
entries.rationale: Mi Quang 1A turns a known dish into a practical restaurant stop through bowl choice, herbs, cracker, and a short lunch rhythm.

sections.title: A Fast Table For A Focused Bowl
sections.body: Mi Quang 1A keeps the meal narrow: sit down, choose the bowl style, fold in the herbs, and let the day keep moving.

sections.title: Know The Bowl Style
sections.body: This is not the moment for a broad Da Nang dinner. Keep the order around mi Quang and decide chicken, shrimp-and-pork, or whatever house version is available.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Mi Quang 1A is easiest to remember as a small noodle-shop table: herbs, cracker, and a focused bowl before the day keeps moving.

sections.title: Herbs Do Some Work
sections.body: The greens, peanuts, sauce, and cracker are part of the balance. Taste once before adding more heat, then fold the herbs through instead of leaving them beside the bowl.

sections.title: Noodle Stop, Not Big Dinner
sections.body: Good when the plan is a focused bowl rather than a broad dinner. Choose the mi Quang first, then add sides only if the table rhythm is clear.

sections.title: Short Meal, Clear Memory
sections.body: This kind of noodle stop fits a day with river light, beach time, or a museum already on it. It gives local flavor without turning lunch into a long sit.

entries.summary: Da Nang Museum is the city-first culture stop for local history, regional context, riverfront civic space, and an indoor pause away from beach-and-bridge plans.
entries.context: The museum is useful when Da Nang has only meant coast, bridges, seafood, and traffic so far. Check hours and tickets before planning the indoor pause.
entries.tip: Pick one thread before reading every wall: city history, wartime context, or regional culture. A focused route keeps the visit from becoming a checklist.
entries.rationale: Da Nang Museum gives the city itself the first word, then pairs naturally with a Bach Dang or Han River walk afterward.

sections.title: The City Gets The First Word
sections.body: Da Nang Museum is the counterweight to a beach-and-bridge trip. Go in for the city itself: riverfront civic space, local history, regional culture, and enough indoor quiet to reset the day.

sections.title: Pick One Thread
sections.body: Choose city history, wartime context, or regional culture before reading every wall. A short museum visit feels better when you leave with one clear thread instead of ten half-read rooms.

sections.title: Bach Dang Changes The Exit
sections.body: The riverfront location makes the after-museum move easy: step back into daylight, walk the Han River side, and let bridges and traffic make more sense with some city context behind them.

sections.title: Quiet Beats Completion
sections.body: This is an indoor pause, not a test. Stop at a few objects, skip the rest, and leave while the city still feels sharper.

entries.summary: Da Nang Museum Branch 2 is a quieter culture pause, useful for courtyard light, gallery rooms, display cases, and a few objects rather than a full museum mission.
entries.context: A smaller culture pause than the main museum. Keep the visit modest: courtyard light, gallery rooms, display cases, and a few objects worth noticing.
entries.tip: Let the courtyard slow the visit before the rooms. Pick a few objects or room details instead of forcing a full timeline.
entries.rationale: Branch 2 gives Da Nang a smaller indoor culture stop that contrasts with the outdoor beach, bridge, and seafood rhythm.

sections.title: A Quieter Way Into The City
sections.body: Da Nang Museum Branch 2 is better treated as a small culture pause than another box to tick. Courtyard light, gallery rooms, display cases, and a few objects can give the city more depth.

sections.title: Courtyard First, Rooms After
sections.body: If the visit begins outside, give that light a minute before the display cases. Smaller museum stops are easier when you slow down before trying to read everything.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Bao tang Da Nang - Co so 2 means Da Nang Museum, Branch 2. The name matters because this is a branch-style stop, not the main museum.

sections.title: Pick Objects, Not A Timeline
sections.body: Choose a few objects, artworks, or room details and follow them. Branch museums can lose shape if you force every label into one story.

sections.title: Small Culture Pause
sections.body: Good as a quieter indoor culture stop, with courtyard light and a few objects carrying the visit. Let it stay modest beside the main museum.

sections.title: Bridge-And-Beach Da Nang Gets Quieter
sections.body: The contrast matters: after traffic, river views, and outdoor plans, quiet rooms let the city gather a little depth. Keep the visit short enough that the objects stay clear.

entries.summary: My An is the Da Nang beach-side neighborhood where hotels, cafes, small shops, motorbikes, and midday shade turn a stay into real blocks.
entries.context: The area is not one big sight. It works when someone learns a few corners, return points, and dinner routes around the beach side.
entries.tip: Pick one cafe, hotel, or corner you can find again. My An is easier when a walk has a home base.
entries.rationale: My An makes the beach side feel lived-in, with hotel edges, small shops, cafes, and lanes behind the sand.

sections.title: Read The Beach Side By Blocks

sections.title: Walk Before Choosing Dinner
sections.body: The area makes more sense after one unhurried pass. Notice which cafes have people inside, where the hotel edges thin out, and which lanes feel comfortable after dark.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: My An is the neighborhood name to know around this beach side. It turns cafes, hotel edges, and small streets into something clearer than one blur near the sand.

sections.title: Beach Rhythm, Everyday Streets

sections.title: Neighborhood Base Check

sections.title: A Return Point Matters

entries.summary: My An Beach is a quieter beach-side pause near the My An stay area, with open sand, hotel edges, and a low-friction way onto the coast.

entries.rationale: My An Beach gives Da Nang a softer beach edge that connects naturally to My An without competing with My Khe's bigger-name role.

sections.title: Beach Time With Conditions

sections.title: Sea Air Before Seafood

entries.summary: My Khe Beach gives Da Nang its open coastal scale: wide sand, city behind, sea in front, and a morning that can reset the whole day.
entries.context: Da Nang's recognizable beach stretch, with weather and water still shaping the visit. Let the day decide between swimming, walking, or simply watching the sea.

entries.rationale: My Khe gives Da Nang its beach identity while staying practical about pickup, conditions, and the city's nearness.

sections.title: Go Early For The Wide Beach

sections.title: City Behind, Sea In Front

sections.title: Morning Coastal Reset

sections.title: Weather Changes The Mood

sections.body: Nam House is strongest when the day needs shade, ice, and a room with its own patience. Plants, patterned tiles, vintage corners, and a slow glass make the pause feel chosen.

sections.title: Drink First, Seat Second
sections.body: Order the coffee you actually want first: sweet, black, or milk-forward if available. Then look for the corner that feels easiest.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Nam House usually stays as the venue name. Let the name sit beside plants, patterned tile, old objects, and a slower room.

sections.title: Old-House Details Carry The Pause
sections.body: The room matters here. Patterned tile, plants, old objects, and warm corners give you something to notice while the ice melts and the street heat drops away.

sections.title: Room-Led Coffee Break
sections.body: Good for a short cafe reset when the room matters as much as the drink. Choose simply, sit where the light feels good, then move on.

sections.title: Better As A Reset Than A Camp
sections.body: This is a good short pause between meals, markets, and beach-side heat. Stay long enough to cool down and look around, then let the cafe remain one quiet piece.

entries.summary: Nam O fish sauce village turns nuoc mam into a coastal craft: anchovies, salt, barrels, time, salty air, and everyday Vietnamese flavor.
entries.context: This is not a generic shopping stop. The point is salty air, barrels, anchovies, and why Nam O is tied to fish sauce.
entries.tip: Look for the making before the buying. The smell, barrels, and coastal lanes are part of understanding why Nam O is tied to fish sauce.
entries.rationale: Nam O fish sauce village connects Da Nang's coast, local craft, and a flavor that sits behind many Vietnamese meals.

sections.title: Fish Sauce Starts On The Coast
sections.body: Nam O turns nuoc mam back into a coastal craft: anchovies, salt, barrels, time, and lanes where the smell tells you what is being made.

sections.title: Barrels First, Products Second
sections.body: Look for the making before the shopping. The point is the slow change from fish and salt into sauce, and the village makes that transformation feel physical.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Lang nghe nuoc mam Nam O tells the story in the name: craft village, fish sauce, and the coastal village that gives the stop its reason.

sections.title: The Smell Is Part Of The Visit
sections.body: This is not a polished attraction sealed away from its work. The salty, fermented air is part of understanding why Nam O is tied to fish sauce.

sections.title: Craft Before Shopping
sections.body: Good when the point is understanding fish sauce as a coastal craft. Notice barrels, salt, anchovies, and village lanes before thinking about bottles.

sections.title: Pair Flavor With Shoreline
sections.body: If the day already points toward Nam O, add the reef only when tide and weather make the coast worth seeing. One stop gives flavor; the other gives shoreline.

entries.summary: Nam O Reef is a rocky shoreline stop for tide pools, fishing-village edges, low light, and a different side of Da Nang's coast north of town.
entries.context: A condition-dependent rocky shoreline, not resort sand. Tide, weather, access, and footing shape whether the stop makes sense.
entries.tip: Go only when conditions make the rocks visible and safe enough to read. Watch your footing and keep distance from working coastal space.
entries.rationale: Nam O Reef adds a specific northern-coast nature stop that pairs naturally with the Nam O fish-sauce craft area.

sections.title: Go When The Tide Shows The Rocks
sections.body: Nam O Reef is shoreline, not resort sand. The good version is rocks, tidal pools, fishing-village edges, and low light that gives the coast its shape.

sections.title: Tide Is The Difference
sections.body: The reef matters most when water level reveals texture: dark rock, shallow pools, and small edges that disappear when conditions are wrong. Check tide and weather first.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Ran Nam O is the local reef name. It keeps the stop about rocky shoreline, not a general beach or seafood area.

sections.title: Walk Like It Is Working Coast
sections.body: Treat the shore as a local fishing edge, not a stage set. Watch your footing, keep distance from slick rocks, and give people working near water enough room.

sections.title: Low Tide, Careful Feet
sections.body: Good when tide and weather make the rocks readable. This is a condition-dependent shoreline, better for careful looking than casual resort sand.

sections.title: Add It Only When The Route Fits
sections.body: Pair the reef with Nam O fish sauce village if you are already on this side of Da Nang. It is less convincing when squeezed into a packed beach-and-bridge day.

entries.summary: Nem lui is a hand-rolled table ritual: grilled pork, rice paper, herbs, sauce, and a first order that teaches the meal slowly by hand.
entries.context: A hands-on food stop about wrapping, dipping, heat, and shared table rhythm, with peanut or pork questions handled before the plate gets complicated.
entries.tip: Watch one roll before copying. Ask about peanuts before dipping if that matters, and taste the sauce before adding heat.
entries.rationale: Nem lui is built around motion, sauce, and table confidence, not just a skewer arriving on a plate.

sections.title: Roll The Skewer While It Is Hot
sections.body: Nem lui is a small table ritual: grilled pork, rice paper, herbs, and sauce moving through your hands before the skewer cools. The flavor is in the roll.

sections.title: Watch One Roll Before Copying
sections.body: If staff or another table shows the rhythm, take the hint: pork off the skewer, herbs in, sauce controlled, rice paper wrapped tight enough to hold.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Nem lui is the dish name to remember. In Da Nang, keep it tied to skewers, herbs, rice paper, and sauce rather than plain grilled pork.

sections.title: Sauce Sets The Bite
sections.body: The sauce can make nem lui feel rich, sweet, nutty, or sharper depending on the shop. If peanuts matter, ask before dipping; if heat worries you, taste first.

sections.title: Wrap Slowly
sections.body: Good when the group can slow down and assemble the bite: skewer, herbs, rice paper, sauce, and heat. Ask about peanuts or pork if needed.

sections.title: One Order Is Enough To Learn
sections.body: This is a good first-round dish because it teaches the table without committing the whole meal. Order one portion, understand the roll, then decide what to add.

entries.summary: Nen Da Nang is a composed dinner stop where herbs, ceramics, small courses, staff rhythm, and time matter more than a quick plate.
entries.context: Nen is a slower dinner plan, not a quick plate between stops. Leave room for the booking, table pace, staff guidance, and any food limits.
entries.tip: Leave room around the booking and mention food limits early. A meal like this works better when it is not squeezed between other plans.
entries.rationale: Nen adds a higher-commitment dinner stop to Da Nang through pacing, room for conversation, and a composed table rhythm.

sections.title: A Dinner That Slows The Night
sections.body: Nen is for the Da Nang evening when the meal is meant to hold its own place in the plan. Expect herbs, ceramics, small courses, and staff rhythm.

sections.title: Space Around The Booking
sections.body: Leave room around the booking. A tasting-style meal loses its shape if you are squeezing it between a beach shower, bridge photos, and a late ride.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Nen Da Nang is the venue name to recognize. Tie it to a slower, composed dinner rather than a casual stop between beach and bridge.

sections.title: Food Limits Before Courses
sections.body: If shellfish, pork, heat, alcohol, or a dietary restriction matters, say it before the table starts moving. It is easier to adjust early.

sections.title: Dinner With Intention
sections.body: Good when the meal itself is the evening plan. Leave room for a slower table pace, careful dishes, and staff guidance rather than squeezing it between stops.

sections.title: Dinner Needs Time
sections.body: Nen reads clearly when conversation has time to catch up with the plates. Go with someone who wants dinner to be one of the day's memories.

entries.summary: Ngu Hanh Son District is the south-beach Da Nang area name linking hotel edges, beach roads, cafes, Non Nuoc, and the limestone hills.
entries.context: A south-beach district label for orienting hotels, beach roads, cafes, Non Nuoc, and Marble Mountains, not a single attraction.
entries.tip: The Marble Mountains are the easiest marker. Walk small blocks in heat, then ride between hotel areas, beach roads, and hill-side stops.
entries.rationale: Ngu Hanh Son District turns a broad area label into practical orientation for the south-beach side of Da Nang.

sections.title: The Beach District With Hills Behind It
sections.body: Ngu Hanh Son District is the name to keep in mind when Da Nang shifts south toward hotel edges, beach roads, cafes, Non Nuoc, and the limestone hills.

sections.title: Hold The Hills As Your Marker
sections.body: The Marble Mountains give the area its easiest mental shape. Even near beach buildings or a cafe stretch, the limestone behind the district keeps the map from feeling vague.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Quan Ngu Hanh Son is the district name. It is useful when hotels, beach roads, cafes, and mountain-side stops need one local label.

sections.title: Short Hops Beat Long Wanders
sections.body: Distances can look smaller on a phone than they feel in heat. Walk the block you are on, then ride between hotel areas, the beach, and hill-side stops.

sections.title: Area Name After Check-In
sections.body: Good when a hotel, beach road, cafe block, or Marble Mountains route needs a district label. It is orientation, not a single attraction.

sections.title: After Check-In, The Name Matters
sections.body: The district name earns its place when your stay is nearby. It gives ordinary tasks like coffee, laundry, seafood, a pharmacy, or an evening walk a clearer local label.

entries.summary: Nguyen Hien Dinh Tuong Theatre is a Da Nang stage-night stop for painted faces, masks, drums, curtains, and traditional performance instead of another photo stop.
entries.context: A stage-night stop belongs on evenings with a real performance to build around. Check the program first, then let the ride serve the show.
entries.tip: Confirm the program and start time before crossing town. Arrive early enough to find the doors and settle into the room.
entries.rationale: The theatre gives Da Nang a living performance-culture stop that contrasts with beaches, bridges, and static museums.

sections.title: A Stage Night, Not Another Photo Stop
sections.body: Nguyen Hien Dinh Tuong Theatre gives Da Nang a quieter evening layer: painted faces, masks, music, curtains, and the focus of a small performance room.

sections.title: The Show Comes First
sections.body: Treat this as a theatre plan only when a performance is actually on. Check the evening's program before crossing town.

sections.title: Name To Recognize
sections.body: Nha hat Tuong Nguyen Hien Dinh is the theatre name. Tuong points toward the traditional performance form, not a general modern theatre night.

sections.title: Arrive Show Time Buffer
sections.body: Give yourself enough time to find the doors, sit down, and settle into the room. Traditional theatre is easier when you are not sliding in late.

sections.title: Program Before The Ride
sections.body: Good when the night already has a show in view. Build the ride around the curtain time, then arrive early enough to settle.

sections.title: Watch The Rhythm
sections.body: A little margin changes the night. Arrive early, find the doors, and let the room settle before the drums, masks, and curtains take over.
